newsitem.title: JAPAN: Ex-Hamanaka boss has been Rudolf Wolff consultant.
newsitem.headline: Ex-Hamanaka boss has been Rudolf Wolff consultant.

text.p: The former supervisor of disgraced Sumitomo Corp copper trader Yasuo Hamanaka said on Friday that he has been a consultant for British metal trader Rudolf Wolff for over 10 years, drawing a consultant's fee of at least 10 million yen a year.
Tokyo prosecutors say Saburo Shimizu, who was Hamanaka's supervisor at Sumitomo Corp in the late 1980s, first began racking up losses with Hamanaka through unauthorised trading during that period.
Shimizu resigned from Sumitomo in the late 1980s.
Shimizu, who was summoned on Friday to speak at Hamanaka's ongoing trial on fraud and forgery charges, said he has been a consultant for the British metals broker.
"I've been a consultant for Rudolf Wolff since leaving Sumitomo," he told the court.

Hamanaka, for many years the most influential trader in the world copper market, has pleaded guilty to charges of fraud and forgery in connection with unauthorised trades that Sumitomo blames for a $2.6 billion copper market loss.
He faces a maximum 15 years in prison under the charges.
